new.story: A two rupees from the India of 2014, part of the series launched in 2011 to carry the rupee's new symbol - the sign that blends the Latin R with the Devanagari RA, adopted in 2010 to give the currency a mark of its own like the dollar or the pound. It sits above the big 2, with lotus flowers curling up both sides. The other face carries the Lion Capital of Ashoka, the four lions of the emperor's pillar that India took as its state emblem, with the country's name in Hindi on the left and English on the right and the motto Truth Alone Triumphs beneath. The small dot under the date marks it as a product of the Noida mint, outside Delhi.
new.notes: Both sides photographed in the holder. Transcription from the coin: obverse BHARAT in Devanagari at the left, INDIA at the right, SATYAMEVA JAYATE below the Lion Capital; reverse the rupee symbol over a large 2 between lotus sprays, date 2014 below with a small round dot mint mark beneath it, read clearly in an enhanced crop - the round dot is Noida (Mumbai strikes a diamond, Hyderabad a star, Kolkata none). Stainless steel, bright, with light circulation wear.
